name: Tindra Cloudberry-Cardamom Frost
manufacturer: Tindra Artisan Beverages (small-batch independent, Tier 4 positioning)
description: A limited-production sparkling drink using real cloudberry extract — one of the rarest fruit sources in M88's supply chain — paired with hand-ground cardamom and still water from a Great Lakes deep aquifer. Sold in small-batch numbered bottles.
flavor_profile: Delicate, honey-apricot cloudberry with warm, resinous cardamom spice, very fine bubbles, almost wine-like complexity, clean mineral finish from the aquifer water
slogan: From the edge of the growing world.
cultural_context: Tindra is the soda you bring when you want to impress without looking like you're trying too hard. It occupies an interesting space: too expensive for Tier 3 everyday consumption but too approachable (it's still just a soda) for Tier 5 prestige signaling. Tier 4 corporate entertainment budgets love it. The numbered bottles have become minor collectibles.
story_hooks: Tindra's cloudberry source is a semi-wild cultivated patch in the northern Great Lakes corridor managed by a small collective — the collective has just discovered the land they operate on is technically owned by a corponation, and the legal situation is about to become very complicated.

Bottle number 1,000 of a recent Tindra run was supposed to be gifted to a Tier 5 executive as a promotional gesture — it went missing in transit, and the circumstances of its disappearance suggest something more than a logistics error.

A food scientist who worked briefly for Tindra claims the 'deep aquifer' water is actually processed municipal water with added mineral compounds — the truth of this allegation, and who is funding the scientist's new platform, is unclear.
